A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Renamed datasets and material moved between the appendices and main text can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments on shipwreck sonar, CUB, and synthetic datasets, including quantitative comparisons and qualitative results in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds SAS-Clutter segmentation results, including a quantitative comparison using approximately 200 annotated objects.

M1.justification: The masking network, background clustering, counterfactual construction, EBSW divergence, background loss, and optional SAS+dSprites quantile loss remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the training procedure without establishing an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: V2 adds SAS-Clutter: approximately 10,000 real synthetic-aperture sonar snippets containing small seafloor objects such as traps, barrels, and tires. This substantially extends real-object evaluation beyond shipwrecks; v1's SAS+dSprites used artificial objects. AI4Shipwrecks is the renamed SSS dataset.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the retained experiments. SAS-Clutter extends the same ILSGAN, ReDO, and Savarese et al. comparator set already evaluated on shipwrecks, rather than introducing additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: The new SAS-Clutter protocol specifies approximately 200 annotated validation objects, 2,000 held-out test objects, normalization and resizing, and best-iteration versus convergence scoring for Savarese et al. Existing experimental protocols are retained. IoC terminology is replaced by IoU/Jaccard wording, without evidence that retained scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: Section 6.2 adds a limited SAS-Clutter error analysis covering dilated object highlights, eroded shadows, and the inpainting baseline's deterioration between its best iteration and convergence. Existing clustering sensitivity studies and appendix failure examples are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Existing aggregate ± reporting is retained, and SAS-Clutter adds further results using that reporting style. No new stated uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run count, seed protocol, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Section 6.2 adds substantive real-SAS evidence: IoU 0.46 ± 0.18 for the proposed method versus 0.36 ± 0.14 at the inpainting baseline's best iteration and 0.21 ± 0.15 at convergence, alongside qualitative masks and reported GAN failures. Corresponding shipwreck, CUB, and synthetic-data scores remain unchanged; these are new benchmark results, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds explicit finite-sample conditional distributions using Dirac measures and formal minibatch divergence definitions supporting Algorithm 1. This is a limited formal extension; the population assumptions, nondegeneracy argument, existing losses, and Appendix B derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim weakly supervised segmentation through background-conditioned counterfactual matching without pretrained networks or adversarial training, with successful sonar applications and qualified natural-image performance. The new conclusion consolidates these contributions, while SAS-Clutter supplies additional supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the explanation of CUB failures: plausible counterfactuals can omit bird parts, create bird-like silhouettes, or retain contextual background objects despite inaccurate masks. It also revises clustering limitations, removes the earlier sliced-Wasserstein phase-insensitivity explanation, and discusses possible extensions using limited ground-truth masks and copy-paste supervision.

D1.justification: V2 documents cluster-wise minibatch construction in Algorithm 1, clarifies that shipwreck preprocessing produces 71,500 crops, and describes SAS-Clutter collection, adjacent-background selection, and preprocessing. It explicitly states that SAS-Clutter is not public. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, and code-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dvornik et al. (2018), Dwibedi et al. (2017), and Fang et al. (2019), connecting the work to contextual object placement and copy-paste supervision. The broader research positioning and Appendix A taxonomy remain stable; most other reference edits concern bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: Data and Implementation Details become separate main sections, synthetic-data results move into the main Results section, and a standalone Conclusion is added. The problem formulation and discussion receive expanded explanations, alongside widespread copyediting and consistent dataset naming.

P2.justification: V2 adds a notation table, Algorithm 1, and the SAS-Clutter figure. It relocates several synthetic-result displays and the large CUB counterfactual grid from appendices into the main text, reformats the cluster-performance plot and tables, and reorganizes appendix figure placement. Most underlying visual results are retained.

improvement.justification: The real SAS-Clutter evaluation strengthens the sonar evidence, while explicit training documentation and the expanded CUB discussion improve clarity and explain important limits of the objective. These gains extend an already supported method rather than resolve a fundamental deficiency. Their strength is bounded by SAS-Clutter's nonpublic availability and approximately 200 annotated objects; established benchmark results remain unchanged.
